references.text: Ezra did not lift his face to God in shame over sin: 'My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift my face to you, my God' ([ref:Esra 9:6|Ezra 9:6]). The same attitude as the tax collector who would not lift his eyes to heaven.
David's prayer for mercy in [ref:Sal 51:3-5|Psalm 51:3-5] is a sinner's humble plea for forgiveness, just as the tax collector prays 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner'.
'A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise' ([ref:Sal 51:19|Psalm 51:19]). The tax collector shows precisely such a broken heart in his humble prayer.

Lifting one's eyes to God and asking for mercy is the theme of [ref:Sal 123:1-2|Psalm 123:1-2], where the praying person looks up to the Lord as a servant looks at their master, dependent on his grace.

'Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord … If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who could stand?' ([ref:Sal 130:1-4|Psalm 130:1-4]). A confession of sin and plea for mercy similar to the tax collector's prayer.
God dwells with the one who is crushed and lowly in spirit ([ref:Jes 57:15|Isaiah 57:15]). The tax collector represents the humble and brokenhearted whom God cares for.
'To this man I will look, to the poor and crushed in spirit, and one who trembles at my word' ([ref:Jes 66:2|Isaiah 66:2]). The tax collector's attitude is exactly what God looks upon with favor.
Daniel's prayer in [ref:Dan 9:18-19|Daniel 9:18-19] appeals not to his own righteousness, but to God's great mercy – the same fundamental attitude as the tax collector who asks for grace.
Jesus concludes in [ref:Luk 18:14|Luke 18:14] that the tax collector went home justified, not the Pharisee – 'whoever humbles himself will be exalted'.
At the cross, the crowd beat their breasts ([ref:Luk 23:48|Luke 23:48]), the same gesture used by the tax collector as an expression of grief and repentance.

The call to come boldly before the throne of grace to receive mercy ([ref:Hebr 4:16|Hebrews 4:16]) corresponds to the tax collector's prayer that God would be merciful to him – God's gracious answer to the sinner's cry.
